newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto sees more gene-altered crops in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto sees more gene-altered crops in 1997.

text.p: Protests over the use of genetically altered crops have had little impact on consumer confidence, and should not stop growth in acreage devoted to herbicide-resistant soybeans or pest-resistant corn, an official of drug company Monsanto Co said.
"There could be as much as 10 percent of next year's corn crop in Bt production," Dr Molly Cline, Monsanto's director of food industry relations, told an industry conference on Sunday.
Monsanto already produces herbicide-resistant Roundup Ready soybeans. It will have corn that includes the Bt protein, resistant to the European corn borer, available to producers this year.

Citing a Monsanto-sponsored survey of 1,058 farmers who planted the genetically altered soybeans in 1996, Cline said 53 percent said they would plant again next year. About 32 percent said they would probably plant Roundup Ready soybeans again.
Many were waiting for final yield data before making 1997 planting decisions, she said.
The use of Roundup Ready soybeans has drawn worldwide protests from environmentalists and critics who say that genetically altered crops have no place in the food chain.
However, most regulatory bodies in Europe, Japan and the U.S. have determined that soybeans are safe for feed and food usage. But the European Union has not given approval for the use of Bt corn.
"Acceptance will vary by country, but for most consumers there are bigger (food safety) issues," Cline said.
According to a survey sponsored by the U.S. trade group the Food Marketing Institute, consumers in the U.S. said spoilage and pesticide residues are the top food safety concerns.
